what: The Fuel Cost Calculator works out how much fuel a trip needs and what it costs, from the distance, your car's fuel economy and the fuel price. It understands kilometers and miles, liters and US or UK gallons, and every common economy unit: L/100 km, km/L and mpg.
It works for electric cars too, using kWh per 100 km or miles per kWh and the price per kWh. Split the cost between passengers to see what each person owes.
uses: Budget fuel for a holiday drive.
Split the fuel cost fairly between riders.
Work out the monthly cost of driving to work.
See how much a more efficient car would save on the same trip.
tutorial: Type the distance, pick km or miles, and choose one way or round trip.
Type your car's economy and choose its unit, such as L/100 km, km/L or mpg.
Type the fuel price and choose whether it is per liter, US gallon or UK gallon. For electric cars it is per kWh.
Pick your currency and how many people share the cost.
See the trip cost, cost per person, fuel needed and cost per km and mile.
features: L/100 km, km/L, US mpg and UK mpg.
kWh/100 km, km/kWh, mi/kWh and Wh/mi.
Doubles the distance in one click.
Splits the total between any number of people.
Warns when the economy looks wrong for a car.

example.title: Worked example: a 250 km trip
example.text: A car uses 7 L/100 km and fuel costs 1.60 per liter. One way, 250 km needs 17.5 L and costs 28.00. As a round trip shared by 4 people it is 56.00, or 14.00 each, which is 0.11 per km.

tips: Real-world economy is usually 10–20% worse than the official figure.
Highway driving is often more economical than city driving.
Measure your actual economy with the Mileage Calculator.
problems: The cost looks far too high or low
Check the economy unit: 7 L/100 km and 7 km/L are very different.
You picked an electric economy unit; electricity is priced per kWh.
They use different gallons. Choose the one that matches your source.
